title: Lampard looking to build on 'pleasure' of Coventry's first Premier League win
subtitle: Coventry City are looking to make it back-to-back wins in the Premier League when they welcome Newcastle United to CBS Arena.
paragraphs: Frank Lampard says it was a relief for Coventry City to earn their first Premier League win but admitted there is still work to do ahead of facing Newcastle United.

Coventry lost each of their first four Premier League matches following their promotion without scoring a goal but ended both droughts with their 1-0 victory over Nottingham Forest before the international break.
It was a first top-flight win in 25 years, but Lampard's side have slipped down to 19th in the table following the rest of the weekend's results.

Only against Crystal Palace (five) has Lampard won more Premier League games as a manager than he has versus Newcastle (three), and he is confident he can add to that tally, as long as Coventry continue to build on their progress.
"It was really a relief and a real pleasure as it sunk in for the players to feel that feeling of winning a Premier League game," Lampard said.

"I have to understand why, [for] the players, that's a big deal for them, so as long as we remember all the reasons why they got there and keep doubling down on all the work we're talking about and what we do, then it's good.
"There will be things that they will naturally learn as they go, and my job is to be there to support them and understand if they keep going, keep working, belief will grow with that."
Newcastle, meanwhile, sit 11th in the table, having lost just one of their five league matches under Matthias Jaissle so far.
They responded well to their resounding 4-1 defeat to Leeds United, heading into the break on the back of a 2-1 win over high-flying Hull City.
Jaissle is not getting ahead of himself just yet, though, and is wary of the threat that a buoyant Coventry can pose to the Magpies.
"Every team is capable of winning against every opponent," Jaissle said.
"Coventry have the momentum, as they won their last match, and confidence. They also have quality and a clear playing style.
"If we perform at our best, then it will be difficult to beat us. We want to make it as difficult for them as possible."
Coventry City – Jay Dasilva
Jay Dasilva scored Coventry's first Premier League goal of the season and scored on his 127th appearance across all competitions.
His goal ended a run of 599 minutes without a goal in the Premier League for Coventry.
Newcastle United – Lewis Hall
Only Kobbie Mainoo (40) has won possession more times than Lewis Hall (38) in the Premier League this season.
Hall also ranks top among all full-backs/wing-backs for carries (64) and carry distance (803.5m).
MATCH PREDICTION: NEWCASTLE UNITED WIN

Coventry have lost seven of their last eight league games against Newcastle (W1), including their last five in a row. This is the first time the two sides will face each other in the league since 2009-10 in the Championship, and first in the Premier League since 2000-01.
Newcastle won both of their last two league visits to Coventry by 2-0 scorelines in September 2000 and December 2009 but have never won three in a row before.
Coventry have struggled at home this term, as well, losing both such league games by an aggregate score of 0-6.

Only five sides in the competition's history have lost each of their opening three home matches of a campaign without scoring: Everton in 2005-06 and 2023-24, Crystal Palace in 2017-18, Burnley in 2020-21 and Wolves in 2021-22.

Since the start of May, only Arsenal (eight) and Manchester City (seven) have won more Premier League games than Newcastle (four), who are looking to win successive games in the competition for the third time in 2026, after doing so in January and in March.
